jsonld.site_description: Find every civic district that covers a point or address in Oklahoma, and who represents you there.
jsonld.app_description: Click any point in Oklahoma, or search an address, to see every civic district that contains it, and who represents you there — county, Oklahoma Senate, Oklahoma House and U.S. House districts, cities and towns, school districts and ZIP codes.
jsonld.keywords: Oklahoma district map, what district am I in, Oklahoma Senate district, Oklahoma House district, Oklahoma congressional district, Oklahoma school district lookup

source.people: None yet — identity only. Every Oklahoma county elects three commissioners from three districts (19 O.S. 321); the state Department of Transportation publishes the districts and the State Election Board the names, and neither is wired in this first change. Recorded as gap ok-commissioner-districts.

layers.label: School District (Unified)
layers.rank_note: 415 unified districts, live from TIGERweb (no data/app file); with the 91 elementary districts they cover the state exactly

source.answers: The public school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), queried live at runtime; 415 features for Oklahoma, measured 2026-10-09.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND THE CARD NAMES THE DISTRICT ONLY. Oklahoma's school boards are elected, and no statewide roster of their members was established in this pass — recorded as gap ok-school-board-members.
source.applies: Oklahoma — every point outside the 91 elementary districts. The two tilings partition the state: their Census land areas sum to exactly the 77-county total, measured 2026-10-09. TIGERweb's secondary tiling is empty for Oklahoma (0 features).

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 1,058 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas in the state's own bounding box, fetched live by envelope; the layer hides outside Oklahoma

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, queried live at runtime. ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='40'. 1,058 features in Oklahoma's box, measured 2026-10-09.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Oklahoma. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code (Wichita Falls TX gives 76301).

layers.label: School District (Elementary)
layers.rank_note: 91 elementary (dependent) districts, live from TIGERweb; the ground the unified tiling leaves

source.answers: The elementary school district covering the point, where the point is in one.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 2 (elementary school districts), queried live at runtime; 91 features for Oklahoma, measured 2026-10-09.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND THE CARD NAMES THE DISTRICT ONLY. Oklahoma's school boards are elected, and no statewide roster of their members was established in this pass — recorded as gap ok-school-board-members.
source.applies: Oklahoma — the 91 elementary districts, 11,441 km2 of land between them. Everywhere else the unified card is the answer.

layers.label: City or Town
layers.rank_note: 600 incorporated cities and towns, live from TIGERweb

source.answers: The city or town containing the point, if any.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), queried live at runtime; 600 features for Oklahoma (165 cities, 435 towns), measured 2026-10-09.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Oklahoma's cities and towns elect councils and town boards, and no statewide roster was read in this pass; the card names the place and links nothing it has not verified. Recorded as gap ok-municipal-officeholders.
source.applies: Oklahoma — statewide. A point outside every city and town is unincorporated, which the card states.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-10-09: 634 points in Oklahoma's envelope, under the service's 2,000-record cap today, and paged anyway so that stops being a fact anyone has to re-check.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Oklahoma — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: the State Capitol, Oklahoma City, Oklahoma County

negative_point.note: near Gainesville, Cooke County, TEXAS, about 15 km south of the Red River — outside Oklahoma and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate (minLat 33.50) so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-10-09: TIGERweb's state layer names Texas at this point (control: the Capitol anchor returns Oklahoma). TEXAS BECAUSE NO INSTANCE SERVES IT, and on land rather than on the Red River, whose channel the county fabric could place on either side.
